concept.name: Flash loan
concept.definition: A flash loan is an uncollateralized loan that must be borrowed and repaid (plus fee) within a single blockchain transaction; if repayment does not complete, the entire transaction reverts as if the loan never happened.
concept.intuition: It is a loan that exists only for the duration of one atomic operation — millions of dollars, no collateral, but you must hand it back before the transaction closes or everything unwinds.
concept.mechanics: The borrower contract calls the pool (e.g. Aave's flashLoanSimple), receives the funds, executes arbitrary logic (arbitrage, liquidation, collateral swap), and the pool pulls back principal plus fee (~0.05% on Aave) at the end of the same transaction; failure to approve repayment reverts all state changes. Atomicity makes the loan risk-free for the lender.
concept.failure_modes: Flash loans supercharge exploits: attackers borrow huge capital to manipulate thin DEX prices or oracle feeds, drain vulnerable protocols, and repay in the same transaction — the loan is a tool, and most famous 'flash loan attacks' exploited other contracts' logic, not the lender.
concept.misconceptions: Flash loans do not give free money — the borrowed capital must be repaid in the same transaction, so profit must come from a real opportunity executed atomically. The lender is not the party at risk in flash-loan attacks.
concept.example: Borrow 10,000 ETH via Aave flash loan, buy an asset priced at $1.00 on exchange A, sell it at $1.10 on exchange B, repay 10,005 ETH (0.05% fee) — all in one transaction; if any leg fails, the whole transaction reverts and the loan never existed.
